module_title: Complex Mechanisms, The Pacemaker, and Blood Pressure
introduction: This level focuses on the technical and numerical parameters of human physiology, from where the most challenging competitive exam questions are framed.

core_concepts.title: Blood Pressure (BP)
core_concepts.description:
Normal Blood Pressure: **120/80 mmHg** 
- 120 (Systolic): The pressure when the heart contracts and pushes blood out. 
- 80 (Diastolic): The pressure when the heart relaxes and fills with blood. 
Measuring Instrument: **Sphygmomanometer**.

core_concepts.title: The Natural Pacemaker
core_concepts.description: The heart needs an electrical impulse to beat continuously. This impulse is generated by a specialized cluster of cells located in the right atrium called the **SA Node (Sinoatrial node)**. It is universally known as the natural pacemaker of the heart.

core_concepts.title: Blood Groups and Transfusion
core_concepts.description:
Discovered by Karl Landsteiner. 
- **Universal Donor: O Negative (O-)** (Can donate blood to absolutely anyone, as it lacks A, B, and Rh antigens). 
- **Universal Recipient: AB Positive (AB+)** (Can receive blood from anyone).

core_concepts.title: Carbon Monoxide Poisoning
core_concepts.description: Hemoglobin loves Oxygen, but it loves 'Carbon Monoxide (CO)' **250 to 300 times more**. If CO is present in the air (e.g., from car exhaust or a burning coal fire in a closed room), hemoglobin drops oxygen and binds to CO permanently, leading to death by asphyxiation.

important_entities.name: Pancreas
important_entities.significance: The pancreas is an Exocrine gland (because it secretes digestive enzymes via ducts) AND an Endocrine gland (because it secretes the hormone 'Insulin' directly into the blood). Hence, it is known as a Mixed Gland.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation: Exam Trap: The 'Appendix' is attached to the large intestine. In herbivorous animals (like cows), it houses bacteria to digest raw cellulose. However, in humans, it is a 'Vestigial Organ' (an evolutionary leftover that currently has no primary function).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: To push blood out to the entire body, the heart has to work hard, generating high pressure (120). When relaxing, the pressure drops (80).

exam_strategy_tips: Consistently asked in NDA/CDS and Banking exams: 'Which instrument is used to measure human blood pressure?' Answer: Sphygmomanometer.
